taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO and ITIS accept Malvaviscus arboreus var. drummondii at variety rank. Joey's source overlay uses Malvaviscus arboreus; the project reconciles the local Central Texas plant to var. drummondii.
look_here_first: Look for the flower architecture: five red petals remain tightly furled rather than spreading flat, while the staminal column and style project conspicuously beyond them. Then confirm the stellate-hairy, cordate to shallowly 3-lobed leaves.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 2026-10-14 corrected two-county status: Hays, Travis inside 24-county zone; Williamson outside. Third accepted native county not yet established. Original evidence retained in range_audit.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: The local Joey frame is morphology evidence, not the sole native-range basis.

best_field_traits: stellate hairs on stems and leaf veins
bright red hibiscus-like flowers whose petals remain tightly furled
inferior? no — superior multi-carpellate ovary typical of Malvaceae; avoid confusing the projecting staminal column with the style alone
fleshy red segmented fruit at maturity
morphology_keys.flower: Five petals stay wrapped/furled; numerous stamens are united into a conspicuous staminal column surrounding the style.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Broadly ovate to cordate, often shallowly 3-lobed, coarsely serrate-crenate, palmately veined and stellate-hairy.
morphology_keys.fruit: Fleshy red schizocarp-like fruit composed of multiple mericarps.
joey_field_notes: Joey's San Marcos River video first shows the whole shrub and leaf form, then a close-up labeling the stigma, stamens, and staminal column.
This is one of the strongest local teaching examples for the Malvaceae staminal column.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Turk's cap flowers do not open flat like most Hibiscus; the petals remain rolled around the reproductive column. Local wild material should be kept separate from ornamental color forms unless provenance is known.
